legacy_root.title: Vendor licence riders and their propagation into a redistributed package
legacy_root.question: Which candidate dependencies carry a non-OSI rider (for example a no-ML-training / no-eval-folding clause or a field-of-use restriction), does that rider propagate to a package that merely VENDORS the dependency versus one that only calls it over a local socket, and which of our planned distributions would violate it?
legacy_root.answer: Of the candidate set actually fetched for this unit, mcp_agent_mail is the live in-estate OSI+rider: MIT plus an OpenAI/Anthropic Restricted-Party field-of-use clause that also defines use to include executing and folding the Software into a training corpus or evaluation harness. That rider attaches when the Software (or a Derivative Work) is vendored, linked into a shipped artifact, or published inside a marketplace package. A package that only calls a user-local MCP/HTTP socket does not redistribute the Software, so the rider does not attach to that client. This worktree does not vendor mcp_agent_mail source; current planned marketplace and worktree distributions therefore do not violate it. jsonschema (pinned in this program's CI) is plain MIT — the extractor reports NO rider, which is the catalog negative control. Llama 3.1, named as a CNL-0005 council seat, is a non-OSI licence with a 700 million MAU additional-commercial field-of-use and an incorporated AUP, not an OSI rider, and it does not carry the Llama-3 no-training clause. SUCCESS:RES-0136
legacy_root.schema_note: Catalog output_schema command-center/schema/research-claim-record.schema.json is absent on this worktree (RES-0001). This record is JSON-parseable with state=SUCCESS and carries claim, lineage, Sherman-Kent, two-signal, verbatim-quote, and per-act propagation fields. No ADV rebuild of that schema was attempted.

negative_control.verbatim: NEGATIVE CONTROL: include one dependency with a plain OSI licence and confirm the extractor reports NO rider — an extractor that finds a rider everywhere is matching prose, not clauses. jsonschema COPYING is that OSI licence. The naive word 'restriction' fires on MIT's 'without restriction'; the clause extractor does not.

mcp_agent_mail.why: A client that speaks MCP/HTTP to a separately running local server does not copy the Software into the client package, so the client's distribution is not distribution of the Software. The operator who executes the server is using the Software; if that operator is a Restricted Party, that execution is in-scope of the rider's definition of use. Whether an Anthropic- or OpenAI-directed agent calling a user-owned local process counts as Restricted-Party use is legal-uncertainty, not settled here.
